extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, military lawyers, convening authorities, and commanding officers involved in courts-martial and military disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing courts-martial: recordkeeping, convening authority, review and revision, sentencing, arrests, charges and specifications, punishments, inferior courts, and related evidentiary/pleading requirements in military law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must be full recital of details of trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Is Full Recital of Details of Trial — Even irregular proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record should set proceedings out in proper order, include arraignment, organization, meetings, testimony, close of session, and have a separate record for each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening order must cite authority for each member
rubrics_metrics.description: Convening Order: Authority for each member's acting as such should be cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the convening order shows the authority under which each member sits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate record for each case
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate Record for Each Case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each case must have its own record; do not combine separate cases in one record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death sentence record must state two-thirds vote
rubrics_metrics.description: Death Sentence — Record Must State Two-Thirds Vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When death is imposed the record must expressly state the two-thirds vote supporting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations to clemency not part of record
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to Clemency: Not part of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be more than one recommendation; members should state specific ground; recommendation cannot be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority: identity and situations where original reviewer is defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Who is Reviewing Authority? — Original when convening authority; division commander after merging of separate brigade in division; when accused leaves jurisdiction of convening authority before action on case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who qualifies as reviewing authority in various organizational situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority cannot be restrained by superior authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Can Not be Restrained by Superior Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing authority must exercise its functions without being restrained by a superior authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority cannot delegate functions; jurisdiction same as court
rubrics_metrics.description: Can Not Delegate Functions. Jurisdiction same as that of court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing authority must personally perform its functions and its jurisdiction matches the court's jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority limitations re: general prisoners and discharged offenders
rubrics_metrics.description: Can Not Act on Sentence of General Prisoner if Offense Committed Before Discharge Was Given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies limits on reviewing authority's power as to general prisoners and timing of offenses vs. discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence inchoate until acted on by reviewing authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence Inchoate Until Acted on by Reviewing Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the reviewing authority acts the sentence is not final; the reviewing authority cannot correct the record or add to punishment; it need not approve the finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority cannot correct record or add to punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Can not correct record. Can not add to punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., cannot add punishment by designating penitentiary as 'military prison'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for returning record to court
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for returning record to court — Record materially erroneous; finding 'to the prejudice' on charge of 'conduct unbecoming'; error in time alleged, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of specific grounds upon which a reviewing authority may return the record for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that proceedings are regular
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumption that proceedings are regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent demonstrable defects, proceedings are presumed regular; this informs review and revision standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lost record invalidates sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Record lost — sentence not effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record is lost before action, the sentence will not become effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain irregularities are not fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregularities that are not fatal: misnaming or misdescription of rank when waived; name misspelled but idem sonans; no time pleaded; use of old serial number of charge; hostility of judge advocate to accused; accused shackled during trial; member acted as interpreter; revealing finding of sentence to clerk; omission of adjournment; preparation of record by judge advocate when reporter appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates many non-fatal defects; each may be waived or considered harmless depending on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations when testimony is conflicting
rubrics_metrics.description: When testimony is conflicting: Court's conclusions have weight; a sentence to be valid must rest upon an approved guilty finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should give weight to court conclusions but ensure approved findings support sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for disapproval of sentence (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for disapproval: court denied request of accused for material witness; presence on revision of member who did not sit on hearing; material variance in name between specification and sentence; accuser was prosecuting witness and interpreter; member present at finding absent during substantial part of trial; member acted as judge advocate; court refused to allow witness to correct testimony; limit of solitary confinement exceeded; sentence of confinement did not designate period; sentence requires reviewing officer to fix date of discharge; court excepted material allegation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed list of defects that have been held to justify disapproval of sentence; used to assess validity of convictions/sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of disapproval
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of disapproval: Of conviction — has effect of acquittal. Of acquittal — (treatment differs). Exceeds legal limit — legal portion approved. Mitigation: reasons for (e.g., protracted arrest; mutiny under provocation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains consequences when reviewing authority disapproves convictions/sentences and when mitigation may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits on changing action
rubrics_metrics.description: Action changed before notice — not after. Dismissal irrevocable after execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies temporal limits for altering reviewing action and the irrevocability of certain punishments post-execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penitentiary sentence designation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Penitentiary sentence — designation must be approved by Secretary of War. 'In such place as the reviewing authority may direct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designating penitentiary confinement requires higher approval; reviewing authority cannot unilaterally designate certain places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgating order content and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Promulgating Order: Should give date of action; notice otherwise than by publication of order; should be sent to commanding officer if accused has passed out of the command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders promulgating reviewing action must include date and appropriate notice routing for the accused's current commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority may recommit illegally released prisoner
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing Authority May Recommit a Prisoner Who Has Been Illegally Released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes recommittal by reviewing authority where release was illegal.

rubrics_metrics.name: President as reviewing authority: powers and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may be original and final reviewing authority: Act must be personal (need not have sign manual). May return proceedings for revision; may remit penitentiary sentence at any time; words 'approved' and 'confirmation' equivalent; cannot correct sentence or add to punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the President's unique reviewing powers and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision by Judge Advocate General — standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision by Judge Advocate General: In sentence of reimbursement — Not Necessary That All the Items Should Be Proven. Presumption is that proceedings are regular; facts in record cannot be contradicted except by record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JAG review respects record presumptions and allows some discretion in reimbursement item proofing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities that do not invalidate proceedings (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregularities that do not invalidate the proceedings: charges not referred by convening authority; convening order dated on Sunday; incorrect but sufficient description of accused; failure to comply with one hundredth article of war, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists procedural defects that generally will not void proceedings absent material prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fatal defects (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fatal Defects: Record must show affirmatively whatever is made essential by statutes; officer sits as member after relief; court excused judge advocate and required member to act as such; error discovered after dissolution of court — procedure declared inoperative and withdrawn; court declined a written statement from accused; no finding on the charge; court without jurisdiction to sentence; convening order null; court and judge advocate not sworn; record did not show right to challenge extended; trial for fraudulent enlistment — charges failed to allege receipt of pay; less than five proceed; soldier already discharged when second sentence approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates defects considered fatal to the validity of proceedings and is used to determine mandatory reversal or disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for remission
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for Remission: Conviction of perjury on one contradicted witness; finding of offense different from that charged; accused insane during trial; accused had accomplice who gave evidence against another in a similar case; sentence excessive and exceptional; disregard by court of statement by accused in extenuation of plea of guilty; accused through ignorance did not exercise right of challenge; court recommends clemency and new evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists grounds upon which reviewing authority may remit or mitigate punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of record after confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Loss of Record: After confirmation of sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses consequences and procedures when records are lost after confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal courts identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegal Courts: Civilian convened court-martial; unauthorized officer convened court-martial; authorized convening officer but court constituted illegally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such irregular constitutions render the court illegal and its proceedings subject to disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of executed legal sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal Sentence Irrevocable After Execution: Military courts not part of the judiciary; executed legal sentence cannot be changed or pardoned by Executive or by Congress; mere irregularities do not alter this principle; too late to urge that sentence was not supported by evidence, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once legally executed, sentences are final and not subject to later executive or legislative nullification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal sentence when offense not military
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegal Sentence: When offense is not a military one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the underlying offense is not military in nature, the sentence is illegal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferior courts-martial limits and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Inferior Courts‑Martial: Regimental Court has no authority to punish officers; Garrison Court — President as commanding officer may act on case; Commanding Officer may be accuser; Summary Court limitations (cannot issue process of attachment; no jurisdiction over capital cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines authority and limitations of subordinate military tribunals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary court procedural and appointment constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary court specifics: Summary court officer certifies witness vouchers; post commander — action on record must be personal; may require reconsideration by court; should not appoint himself; summary court officer may be accuser; commanding officer of general hospital may appoint; report of deposited where; summary court officer administers oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural safeguards and appointment practices for summary courts to avoid conflicts of interest and ensure proper records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department commander supervises proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Department Commander Supervises Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher command oversight role in supervising inferior courts and summary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized punishment sources and confinement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Punishment — Authorized: By company commander; by post commander; by sentence of general court-martial. Confinement: begins at date of order promulgating sentence; cumulative sentence; time absent in escape to be made good; prisoners' mail not to be opened; suspended sentence without precedent; good-conduct time; in military prison — prisoners may be required to manufacture articles for sale or issue; all prisoners may be required to work; extent of separation from outside world; private money of general prisoner not subject to forfeiture; guard's authority over prisoner; prisoners required to manufacture clothing; in penitentiary United States must transport men; whole guard responsible that prisoners do not escape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies permissible punishments, administration of confinement, prisoners' rights and duties, and logistical responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized punishments (summary and court-martial examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unauthorized Punishment — Summary: hanging free from ground or immersion in water; striking soldier unnecessarily; 'tied and gagged'; abuse of sentinel; forcing a soldier to contribute to company fund; stopping pay under fifty-fourth article as punishment; for offense of which accused has been acquitted. By sentence of general court-martial — e.g., officer reduction to the ranks (subject to rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of corporal or otherwise unlawful summary punishments and improper punitive practices that are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boards of investigation limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards of Investigation: Can Not Try or Sentence; investigation re case of a dismissed officer; witness fees not allowed; reporter must be authorized by Secretary of War; as to character of enlisted men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes investigatory boards from courts and sets limits on their functions and allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrest — scope and limits for military arrests
rubrics_metrics.description: Military arrests: Authorities are not empowered to make forcible entrance into a private dwelling to effect an arrest of a soldier; arrests may be made in parts of public houses devoted to public purposes; a soldier in arrest should not be fettered except when necessary to prevent violence or escape; status of being in arrest is inconsistent with duty; placing an arrested officer on duty terminates his arrest; arrested in quarters may be required to perform cleaning or police work; release from arrest and requiring duty while awaiting promulgation justified only by extraordinary exigency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets limits on methods of arrest, physical restraints, duties during arrest, and appropriate circumstances for imposing duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrest authority and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Only commanding officers (except in classes indicated in article 24) can place commissioned officers in arrest; arrest is not a privilege of an officer; arrest may be by verbal or written order; reason need not be specified; officer usually required to surrender sword; limits of arrest often the post or quarters unless otherwise stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies who may place officers in arrest, the form of orders, and customary restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation to NCOs for enlisted arrests
rubrics_metrics.description: Company commander may expressly delegate to noncommissioned officers power to place enlisted men in arrest, subject to immediate report to the commander.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation permitted to provide immediate restraint, justified by long service custom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlisted men in arrest: no summary punishment; civil convictions don't bar military trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Soldiers held in military arrest may be subjected to restraint to prevent violence or escape but cannot be subjected to summary punishment. An enlisted man tried and convicted by civil courts and released on parole may be arrested and brought to trial by military authority for military offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects arrested enlisted personnel from summary punishment and permits military jurisdiction for military offenses despite civil conviction/parole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and nature of military offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Military offenses: violations of the laws, orders, or rules of discipline governing the military state; they are neither 'felonies' nor 'misdemeanors' in the civil sense and do not carry felony consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the distinctive nature of military offenses and their legal character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on double pleading and pleading requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Double pleading: specifications alleging multiple distinct offenses (especially under different articles) are properly condemned. A specification should set forth but one instance of offense; there may be one or more specifications to a charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each specification should describe a single instance; double or duplicative pleading may result in disapproval of conviction or sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and essentials of military charge and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A military charge properly consists of technical 'charge' and 'specification' — the charge names the offense; the specification sets forth the facts with time and place. Essentials: 1) laid under the proper article of war or statute; 2) specification sets forth facts sufficient substantially to constitute the offense. Simpler, clear, intelligible English preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly technical or verbose pleadings; ensure the accused can prepare a defense and knows the alleged act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must be appropriate and particular
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification should be appropriate to the charge; if alleging violation of a written order or obligation it should preferably set forth the writing verbatim or state its substance and then detail the act(s) constituting the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches factual allegations to the legal charge and uses the text of written instruments when possible for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accused entitled to know particular act; habit/ general allegations defective
rubrics_metrics.description: The accused is entitled to know for what particular act he is called to account; allegations of general incapacity (e.g., habitual intoxication) or broad charges like 'worthlessness' are defective—should charge specific acts or instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specificity protects fair notice and the ability to prepare a defense; habitual-condition pleadings are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge under wrong article is improper
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an offense is clearly defined in a specific article, it is irregular and improper to charge it under another specific article; conversely, charging under a specific article an offense properly charged under the general article (and vice versa) can be erroneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct statutory article to avoid procedural error and improper punishment scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of willfulness vs negligence where statute distinguishes
rubrics_metrics.description: If an order fixing maximum punishments prescribes different limits for wilfully and negligently allowing a prisoner's escape, a charge should indicate whether the act is alleged to be wilful or negligent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mens rea affects punishments, the specification must allege the appropriate mental state where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joining multiple accused requires concert of action
rubrics_metrics.description: To join several persons in the same charge and bring them to trial together, the offense must require concerted action and have been committed in concert or pursuit of a common intent; mere concurrent acts (e.g., multiple absences) do not suffice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure evidence of conspiracy or concert before charging jointly; otherwise charge separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming conventions in specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not essential to state the full Christian name of an accused; only enough to identify the party unmistakably; where a preferring officer refers to himself as 'me' in a specification against an inferior, the specification should be amended or the preferring officer's name added if objected to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sufficient identification to avoid ambiguity; amend vague self-references where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and place averment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Time and place of the offense should be averred so it may appear the offense was within limitation period and to enable accused to understand the act to defend; where exact time/place unknown, allege 'on or about' or 'at or near' a date or locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'on or about'/'at or near' when exact details unknown; precise averment preferred when known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges may originate with civilians but need authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Military charges may originate with civilians and enlisted men, but charges should be formally preferred by and authenticated with the signature of a commissioned officer; charges from outside should generally be sustained by affidavits or reliable evidence as a condition to adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External complaints require corroboration and proper formal preferral to be actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any officer may prefer charges; prefer to proper convening authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Any officer may prefer charges; an officer is not disqualified because under charges or in arrest. Charges should be preferred to the authority empowered to convene the court for their trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement to present charges to correct convening authority ensures proper processing.
